title: Cloud Adoption Imperative for Life Sciences Organizations
summary: Strategic analysis of cloud adoption drivers in life sciences, including the role of cloud in accelerating new science (novel treatments), data integration, and cross-organization collaboration.

findings.new_science_driver: Novel treatments (high scientific novelty, unmet need, technology convergence) are projected to represent 67% of industry growth. These treatments require diverse data sources, cross-organization collaboration, and computational capabilities that on-premise infrastructure cannot efficiently provide.
findings.data_integration_imperative: Siloed data and incompatible technologies cause significant delays in bringing treatments to market. Cloud platforms enable: unified data lakes across R&D and commercial, real-time analytics on combined datasets, and scalable compute for genomics and real-world evidence workloads.
findings.cloud_as_value_creator: Cloud is positioned not as a cost optimization play but as a value creation enabler — faster time-to-market for treatments, better patient outcomes through data-driven decisions, and new business models built on data sharing and ecosystem collaboration.
findings.compliance_considerations: Life sciences cloud adoption must address: GxP validation of cloud infrastructure, data residency and sovereignty requirements across jurisdictions, 21 CFR Part 11 compliance for electronic records, and vendor qualification for cloud service providers.
findings.ecosystem_collaboration: Cloud platforms enable new collaboration models: sponsor-CRO data sharing for clinical trials, manufacturer-distributor supply chain visibility, and payer-provider outcomes-based contract management.

source: Strategic analysis of the cloud adoption imperative in life sciences covering data integration, new science, and compliance
